messages.subject: Overlay images from dataset
parts:
Hi all again,
I've been looking for this topic on the group but I didnt find it.
I'm trying to make an overlay from 2 differents mz in the same dataset with different combinations.
I use "par" and "image" in this way:

par(mfrow=c(0,0))
image(dataset1, mz=769.28, contrast.enhance="histogram", smooth.image="gaussian", layout=c(1,1), col.regions=alpha.colors(50,"blue"),cex.axis= 0.7, strip=F, colorkey=F)
par(mar=c(0,8,6,3))
image(dataset1, mz=987.09, contrast.enhance="histogram", smooth.image="gaussian", col.regions=alpha.colors(50,"green"), cex.axis= 0.7, strip=F, colorkey=F)
par(mar=c(0,8,6,3))
image(dataset1, mz=804.36, contrast.enhance="histogram", smooth.image="gaussian", col.regions=alpha.colors(50,"orange"), cex.axis= 0.7, strip=F, colorkey=F)
par(mar=c(0,8,6,3))
image(dataset1, mz=757.39, contrast.enhance="histogram", smooth.image="gaussian", col.regions=alpha.colors(50,"purple"), cex.axis= 0.7, strip=F, colorkey=F)
par(mar=c(0,8,6,3))
image(dataset1, mz=1046.54, contrast.enhance="histogram", smooth.image="gaussian", col.regions=alpha.colors(50,"red"), cex.axis= 0.7, strip=F, colorkey=F)

but what I get is not what i want. I get a different image plot for each line, not the overlay. Whats happens to my script?

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Overlay images from dataset
parts:
Hi, sorry for the slow response time. Perhaps you have already figured this out:

To overlay images, you just specify "mz" as a vector, and include "superpose=TRUE".

For example, to recreate the first image from https://ms-imaging.org/wp/imzml/example-files-test/, you would do:

library(Cardinal)

mouse <- readMSIData("/path/to/file.imzML")

image(mouse,
      mz=c(741.5307, 743.5482, 798.541),
      col=c("blue", "red", "green"),
      normalize.image="linear",
      contrast.enhance="suppression",
      superpose=TRUE)

legend("topright",
       fill=c("blue", "red", "green"),
       legend=c(741.5307, 743.5482, 798.541))

Note that you specify "col" instead of "col.regions" to specify categorical rather than continuous color schemes. In the case of overlaid images, Cardinal will automatically add the appropriate alpha levels.

Also, "normalize.image" here is used to rescale the intensities to the same range in order to more easily compare the spatial distributions. Leave it out (or set to "none") to leave the intensities as-is.

-Kylie
